reviewedClaims.correction: Distinguishes Pelargonium from Geranium and zonal, ivy-leaved, regal and scented groups; removes universal uninterrupted flowering promise.
Same growing depth; free drainage holes and suitable substrate. Removed planting to first leaves and gravel drainage layer.
Removed guaranteed May and autumn dates by Latvian region. Uses local forecasts, frost risk, acclimatisation and a clearly attributed approximate +7 C night-temperature guide.

Moisture checks replace a universal interval. No stronger fertiliser dose to compensate for fewer applications. No ash solution or compost-tea replacement recipe. Winter feeding depends on actual growth.

Separates cool bright potted plants, bright living-room plants, rooted cuttings and limited bare-root experiments. No claim that all overwintering needs darkness, no water or a fixed autumn cut to 10–15 cm.

Least reliable method, restricted to suitably mature woody-stemmed plants. Notes different source advice about root soaking; gives no mandatory soaking interval. Does not promise success in Latvian unheated greenhouses or garages.
Healthy nonflowering shoots, clean tools, suitable substrate and moisture while rooting; after rooting, shift to winter care. Removed guaranteed 2–3-week rooting and 'free' promise.
Separates environmental leaf shedding, possible waterlogging, oedema and rust signs. No automatic yellow-leaf diagnosis or blanket pesticide recipe.

sourceLimitations: No Latvian cultivar trial or Latvian-specific overwintering success rate is claimed.
UK and US planting dates, trade compost brands and region-specific chemical products were not transferred.
Cool bright temperatures around 7–10 C are a practical orientation; actual light, growth and moisture govern care.
Sources differ on dormant-root moisture and soaking. The experimental nature is explicit instead of harmonising incompatible instructions into a rigid schedule.
Seed sowing dates and a universal time to first flower were removed rather than extrapolated across all cultivar groups.
